dimension_7_selection_verdict.selection_status: Conditional Operational Selection with Governed Triage
dimension_7_selection_verdict.universal_winner_rationale: No universal candidate model dominates every dimension. HistGradientBoosting delivers the highest grouped-CV ranking (0.4606) and superior cold-start sensitivity (Recall@0.20 = 27.07% vs 19.51% for RF), while Random Forest exhibits slightly superior prospective ranking on 2014J (PR-AUC 0.3093 vs 0.3005) and lower calibration error (ECE 0.0266 vs 0.0420). Linear Logistic Regression is decisively rejected due to catastrophic cold-start collapse.
architectural_justification: 1. Cold-Start Discrimination: HGB's native tree routing handles unobserved prior scores gracefully, capturing 27.07% of failing students under cold start versus only 19.51% for Random Forest and 0.0% for Logistic Regression.
2. Non-Linear Interaction Modeling: Gradient boosting captures non-linear interactions between VLE click recency and cumulative registration timing that linear models miss completely.
3. Operational Governance Integration: Combining HGB with the Module GGG Governance Router (suppressing decoupled practice quizzes and applying tau=0.10 on TMAs) resolves course-specific fragility.
governed_deployment_policy: Deploy HistGradientBoostingClassifier as primary risk-ranking engine.
Enforce ModuleGGGGovernanceRouter to suppress alerts on unweighted self-paced quizzes (GGG CMAs).
Apply dual-threshold operational policy: tau=0.20 for high-stake courses; tau=0.10 for low-prevalence/TMA milestones.
Anchor academic outreach at TMA 3 Capstone milestones where ROC-AUC exceeds 0.81 across all modules.
